# Exact fault-event admission under a fixed local controller

29 October 2026. This package gives an exact noise-conversion operation and
a separate obstruction to an unrepaired clock compiler. It does **not**
establish the missing charged-error memory theorem for the programme's
nominal thermal controller.

## 1. What is fixed and what is unknown

Let the system have finite-dimensional local cells. A catalogue of allowed
error supports has bounded diameter, bounded cardinality and bounded
incidence, all independent of system size. A support can be enlarged to a
known containing cell block; no unknown generator need be estimated. The
nominal local controller, any additional noise deliberately engineered below,
the input encoder and the final receiver are selected before the error.

For the explicit Pauli construction, a catalogue block X contains q_X qubits,
d_X=2^{q_X}, and an unknown time-independent Hermitian term H_X has
||H_X|| <= e_X. Its identity coefficient is immaterial. Additional local
unitary-jump noise can have arbitrary unknown nonnegative rates, with a
specified local total-rate budget. In particular those rates need not obey
detailed balance with any stabilizer Hamiltonian. Such noise is unital;
that fact must not be confused with thermal balance.

Every assertion about an autonomous memory below is conditional on an
explicit **physical-time** fault-event threshold of that controller. Neither
a synchronous threshold, nor a positive average update velocity, supplies
that premise.

## 2. Completing the square: exact coherent-to-unitary-jump admission

Write D_L(rho)=L rho L^dagger-{L^dagger L,rho}/2. For a Hermitian Pauli P,
real h and a positive number l, put

    J=l P+i h I,       r=l+h^2/l,
    U=J/sqrt(l^2+h^2).

Then J^dagger J=(l^2+h^2)I and U is unitary. Literal expansion gives

    (1/l) D_J = l(Ad_P-id)-i h[P,.]

under arbitrarily weak fixed local reset generators and the ensuing quantum

    no neighbor w has c_w=c_v-1 (mod 3).                    (C1)

# Whole review of exact fault-event admission and the clock obstruction

29 October 2026. Root independently read the complete PROOF.md and
CLOCK_OBSTRUCTION.md in c_autonomous_restoring_history. Both arguments are
accepted at their expressly delimited mathematical scope.

The completion-of-the-square normalization, Pauli coefficient l2 bound,
local incidence budget, Choi interior scaling and trace-preserving Poisson
channel identity are correct. The forward admission actually adds a fixed
paid depolarizing ballast; it does not merely unravel the unmodified
Hamiltonian dynamics. The necessary class contains nonunital CPTP events,
which cannot be replaced by random-unitary errors. The minimax statement
is confined to the displayed Pauli completion strategy. Ordinary gauge,
Choi and mixed-unitary tools are credited; the useful result is their
exact application to the remaining controller robustness interface.

For the no-go, the specified six-cycle core stays blocked regardless of
exterior phases; the same six reset channels preserve it. The acquisition
event is independent of quantum data and has a uniform positive conditional
probability from every clock state. The integer-lift invariant bounds
future accepted updates by twice the distance to the core. Its physical
halting bound follows from rate-at-least-one progress until termination.
Thereafter local depolarization contracts entropy relative to the product
maximally mixed state even in the presence of an arbitrary data Hamiltonian
and a reference. Strong subadditivity supplies the complete entropy bound.
Conditioning on past controller records leaves a separable comparison
state after the halt; optimal final recovery cannot restore Bell fidelity.
The stated Fe <= .52 and decoded diamond distance >= .96 are safe.

Scope is essential: all quantum restoration is gated by the unrepaired
classical modular clocks, and no microscopic post-halt bath labels are
given to the receiver. A clock repair layer, independent unclocked recovery
or reliable growing classical memory changes the problem. This is neither
a no-go for autonomous quantum memories nor a charged-error threshold for
the programme's nominal thermal controller. The latter remains open.
